ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a sinusoidal voltage source v_i, with the lower end as the reference line; from the upper end of the source to the right-side output node, the upper branch has a resistor R and a capacitor C connected in series in sequence. Between the right-side output node and the lower reference line there are two parallel branches: one resistor R and one capacitor C. The output v_o is marked across the right-side parallel network, with the upper end positive and the lower end negative. Reasoning: The input is v_i = v_p cos(t/RC), therefore the angular frequency is ω = 1/RC. Using the phasor method, the capacitor impedance is Z_C = 1/(jωC). When ω = 1/RC, Z_C = 1/(j(1/RC)C) = R/j = -jR. The left-side series impedance is Z_series = R + Z_C = R - jR = R(1 - j). The output-end load is the parallel R and C: Z_load = R || Z_C = R || (-jR) = [R(-jR)]/[R - jR] = R(1 - j)/2. The voltage division ratio is V_o/V_i = Z_load/(Z_series + Z_load) = [R(1 - j)/2]/[R(1 - j) + R(1 - j)/2] = (1/2)/(3/2) = 1/3. This ratio is a positive real value, therefore the output is in phase with the input. Thus the steady-state output is v_o = (v_p/3) cos(t/RC).
